newsitem.title: INDIA: Ten killed in rural India caste violence.
newsitem.headline: Ten killed in rural India caste violence.

text.p: At least 10 lower-caste supporters of a communist rebel group were shot dead by gunmen of an outlawed upper-caste security force in the eastern Indian state of Bihar, news agencies said on Monday.
Press Trust of India said one person was wounded in the incident and was admitted in critical condition to Patna Medical College.
The killings took place about 50 km (30 miles) from Patna, the state capital of Bihar, late on Sunday night, PTI reported.

The victims were gunned down in an attack on the village of Kab by more than 100 members of Ranvir Sena, an outlawed private security group formed by upper-caste landlords, the United News of India (UNI) said.
Police have launched a search for the killers, it added.
Those killed were lower-cast supporters of the Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist), UNI said.
Ranvir Sena, a powerful force in central Bihar, has clashed frequently with the communist group, mainly over land disputes.
The communist force is one of many rebel groups considered part of the Naxalite movement, which started in India in the 1960s among groups who split from the main communist party.
It wants a radical redistribution of land in the state, which is bitterly opposed by upper-caste landlords.
